title: Changing one box at a time
idea: When you have two variables, reassigning one does not touch the other. Each box is its own thing. (Numbers only — text as data comes later.)

exercises.prompt:
What will this show (two lines)?

cats = 2
dogs = 4
cats = 5
print(cats)
print(dogs)
exercises.explanation: We only changed cats. dogs was never touched, so it stays 4.

exercises.prompt: Changing the variable 'cats' also changes the variable 'dogs'.
exercises.explanation: No. Each variable is its own box. Changing one leaves the other exactly as it was.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show (two lines)?

first = 1
second = 2
second = 9
print(first)
print(second)
exercises.explanation: Only second was reassigned to 9. first still holds 1.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show (two lines)?

left = 3
right = 3
left = 8
print(left)
print(right)
exercises.explanation: They started the same, but changing left to 8 does not affect right. right stays 3.

exercises.prompt:
Change only the home score to 12, leaving the other box alone.

home = 7
away = 3
home = ____
print(home)
print(away)
exercises.explanation: home = 12 changes just that box. away still holds 3.

exercises.prompt:
After these lines, which statements are TRUE?

apples = 4
bananas = 6
apples = 9
exercises.explanation: apples was changed to 9. bananas was never touched, so it keeps 6.

exercises.prompt: Arrange so it shows 10 then 20 (set both, change only the first, then print both).
exercises.explanation: player1 ends as 10 after its change; player2 stays 20 because we never changed it.

exercises.prompt: Two different variables can hold two different numbers at the same time.
exercises.explanation: Yes! Each box is separate. One can be 1 while another is 9.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show (two lines)?

x = 1
y = 2
x = 3
y = 4
print(x)
print(y)
exercises.explanation: Both boxes were reassigned. x ends as 3, y ends as 4. Each kept its own last value.

exercises.prompt: A friend changed 'score' and expected 'lives' to change too. Why didn't lives change?
options: lives is a separate box — only score was reassigned
You can only change one variable ever
exercises.explanation: Each variable is independent. Reassigning score touches score only. lives keeps its value.
